l.i: nom-
inati:
in Flandria & Arthesia, à loco deserto, ac lupis expositio,
Turrelupini appellati: in Delphinatu fumo cōteptu Chagnardi
dicti, quasi apricarij, quod in locis apricis sine domibus tectisq; desiderent.
Appellatio vero waldensium maxime omnium peruulgata illis remansit, donec
nomen Lutheranorum prolatum, quod inuidia, odio, infamiaq;
cetera omnia opprobria superauit. Sed in his tātis calūnijs & crimi-
nibus, reliquus populus, qui ad pedē Alpiū, & qui Merindolij, Ca-
brieraeque degit, ita pie, ac modeste semper vixit, vt in eorum tota
consuetudine ac vitae ratione, timor Dei maxime cluxerit, summa fides
& iustitia perspecta fuerit.In exigua cognitionis luce, quam Do-
minus eis dederat, in eam vnam curam incumbebant, vt id quod ha-
bebant, magis quotidie accenderent, nullis rebus aut facultatibus suis
parcētes, siue libri Scripturae sacrae parādi[?] essent, siue homines optimo
ingenio praediti, in doctrina pietatis instituendi, siue huc illucq; mittēdi[?],
etiā vsq; ad extremas mūdi partes, vbi aliquē lucis salutaris ra-
diū exortū esse audiuerat.Nā anno M.D.XXX, cum intellexissent,
in quibusdam Germanorum atq; Heluetiorum ciuitatibus Euangelium
annūtiari, ad eas duos ex suis miserūt, Georgiū Maurclū[?], Fresmeriae[?] natū in Delphinatu,
qui apud eos concionatoris munus obibat, homine
pium, & quem in scholis erudiendum informandumque curauerant, & Pe-
trum Latonum Borgundum, vt de fidei pietatisque doctrina cum fi-
delibus ac prudentibus ecclesiarum ministris communicarent, eo-
rumque formam rationemque totam in colendo Deo cognoscerent, ac
priuatim eorum sententiam exquirerent de quibusdam rebus, quae
tum ipsis nonnullam dubitationem adferebant. Quum itaque hi duo
abunde omnia communicassent cum primarijs in Ecclesia Dei viris,
videlicet Basileae cum OEcolampadio, Argentinae cum Bucero &
Capitone, Bernae cum Berktoldo Hallero, ac per Borgundiam reditū
instituissent, Petrus Latomus Diuione captus, in carcerem coniectus
est: Georgius vero solus Merindolium est reuersus, cum libris &
literis ac mandatis, quae ab ecclesijs Germanorum adferebat.Eò autem
cum venisset, omnia legationis suae capita exposuit, eisque declarauit
publice, in quot & quantis erroribus versarentur, in quos veteres ip-
sorum ministri, quos Barbas eorum idiomate, id est, Auunculos
vocabant

page.notes: Left margin: handwritten pencil or ink annotations (names, marks, scribbles) are manuscript additions and were not transcribed. The printed marginal notes are transcribed above. The body is set in italic type, with roman proper names and the notes in roman; the italic setting was read across the whole block and may be partly off. The whole page appears to be one paragraph: no line is indented, and sentences run on without paragraph breaks (e.g. "superauit.Sed", "fuerit.In", "audiuerat.Nā"). The paragraph continues beyond the page end. Doubtful readings: "tātis" and "calūnijs" (marked by macron/tilde reading only); "Maurclū" and "Fresmeriae" (proper names, not certain); "parādi" and "mittēdi" (marked [?] as abbreviations uncertain); "Ministcr" in the note (read as "Minister" but the letters are unclear). The printed text has "Latonum" in the first mention and "Latomus" in the second; both kept as printed. "est:Georgius" has no space in print; a space was added for readability. No page number or catchword is printed.
